transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I can’t seem to let go of this feeling that I’m being punished. It sounds dramatic when I say it out loud, I know, but it’s about my father and how he declined. My sister keeps showing me the doctor’s notes and telling me I did everything I was supposed to do, but it doesn’t really settle anything for me. It feels like some kind of judgment has already been made against me. Does that make sense?
Have you been feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things more than usual, even when others tell you that you did nothing wrong?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to sound like I’m just feeling sorry for myself, but I keep replaying every decision I made about my father’s appointments, like maybe I missed something or pushed the wrong thing. And then I go over tense conversations with my relatives and think I must have been selfish.

It doesn’t really stop there. I start feeling like I’m not just a bad daughter, but… useless at work too. Like I deserve whatever happens because I didn’t do enough. I know people tell me that isn’t fair, but it still feels true. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you find yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself even for things that seem minor or out of your control?

Yes… I mean, I try not to make everything about me, but I do. Even small things turn into proof that I did something wrong.

I keep going back over every decision I made about my father’s appointments, and every tense conversation with my relatives. And somehow I end up feeling like I was selfish, like I was a bad daughter. Then it spreads to work too, like I’m useless there and maybe I deserve whatever happens. I know that probably sounds excessive… but that’s where my mind goes.
Do these feelings of guilt and self-blame come up in other parts of your life, or do they mainly center around your father and family situation?

It started with my father and my family, I think… that’s the main thing. But it doesn’t stay there.

I keep going over every decision I made about his appointments, and every tense conversation with my relatives, and then I sort of decide it means I was selfish, or I failed him somehow. And then at work, even small mistakes make me feel like I’m useless there too… like I deserve whatever happens.

I know that’s probably not a very balanced way to see it. I’m trying to answer honestly, though.
Have these feelings of guilt and worthlessness been present even before your father’s decline, or did they start mainly after those events?

I think it mainly got bad after my father’s decline. I don’t want to say I never blamed myself before, because I’m sure I did sometimes, like anyone does… but this feels different.

Now I keep going back over every decision about his appointments, and every tense conversation with my relatives, and somehow I turn it into proof that I was selfish or failed as a daughter. And then it carries over into work too, like I’m useless there and deserve whatever happens.

I don’t know if that answers it the right way, but… it feels like it really took hold after all of that.
How long have these feelings of guilt, worthlessness, and self-blame been present? Have they been happening every day for at least two weeks or more?

Yes… it’s definitely been more than two weeks. I wish it were just a short patch, but it’s been going on for about a year and two months now, since my father’s health and behavior started changing and I had to step into more of a caregiving role.

It’s not that I’m trying to dwell on it, but the guilt and self-blame have been there most days… pretty much every day, I think. Is that the kind of timeline you mean?
Have these feelings of guilt, worthlessness, and self-blame been present for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two consecutive years, or has it been less than that?

Less than that, yes. It hasn’t been two years.

It’s been… about a year and two months, I think, since my father’s health and behavior started changing and I had to take on more of the caregiving. So it has felt like most days for a long time, but not two consecutive years. Is that the distinction you mean?
Have you noticed that you don’t take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, or that you’ve lost interest in activities that mattered to you before?

I’m not sure I’d say I’ve completely lost interest… I don’t want to overstate it. I still try to do things if I’m supposed to, or if someone asks me.

But I guess I don’t really look forward to much the way I used to. Things that should feel relaxing or nice can feel more like something to get through. I don’t know if that counts as losing pleasure, or if I’m just tired and distracted.
Have you noticed a big drop in your energy, or do you feel more tired than usual, even when you haven’t been doing much physically?

I’m not sure… I mean, I do get tired, but I don’t know if it’s a “big drop” exactly.

Some days I feel worn out even if I haven’t done that much, but I also wonder if that’s just normal stress or not sleeping perfectly or… I don’t know. I can still get through what I need to most of the time, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, feeling restless or unable to sit still?

Maybe a little, yes. I don’t know if I would’ve noticed it as much on my own, but people at work have asked if I’m sick because I guess I’m moving pretty slowly through normal tasks.

And in meetings, sometimes someone asks me something simple and it takes me a second to answer… like there’s a lag. I feel embarrassed saying that. I’m not trying to be difficult or anything. Does that sound like what you mean?
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating much less or much more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

I don’t think so, not in any major way. My appetite maybe varies a bit day to day, but I haven’t noticed a big change or anything I’d call significant.

My clothes fit about the same, as far as I can tell. I haven’t been tracking it closely, though… should I be?
Have you ever had thoughts that life isn’t worth living or that you’d be better off dead, even if you wouldn’t act on them?

Um… I guess, yes, but I don’t want you to think I’m saying I’m going to do something. I don’t have a plan to hurt myself.

It’s more like… on some mornings, especially when I know there are going to be more calls from the care agency and problems waiting at work, I catch myself thinking it would just be easier if I didn’t wake up. I feel awful saying that out loud. But I wouldn’t act on it. Does that make sense?
Would you say that most of your days have felt consistently low or sad since your father’s health started declining, with that feeling lasting throughout most of the day, nearly every day?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is, but most days I wake up with this heavy, kind of hollow feeling.

It’s like the color has gone out of things. I can be sitting at my desk in HR, or even looking out at the garden beds at home, and it just… doesn’t reach me the way it used to. It’s there for a lot of the day, nearly every day, I guess. Is that what you’re asking?
